title: Stomata lie in rows on oblong-celled leaves and scattered on polygonal-celled ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stomata lie in rows on oblong-celled leaves and scattered on polygonal-celled ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because the stomatal mother cell is cut off by a minimal partition whose form depends on epidermal cell shape, stomata are arranged in regular rows where epidermal cells are oblong (as in hyacinth) and irregularly where they are polygonal (as in Sedum).

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is obvious that in the case of the oblong cells of the epidermis in the hyacinth the stomata will be found arranged in regular rows, while they will be irregularly distributed over the surface of the leaf in such a case as we have depicted in Sedum.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Arrangement of stomata”. Scope: leaf epidermis of monocotyledons with oblong cells and dicotyledons with polygonal cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell shape and stomatal spatial order are standard image-derived variables, permitting a strong comparative test. Existing data can test the association in subsets, but the proposed minimal-partition mechanism and broad taxonomic contrast remain confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across leaf epidermal images, quantify cell elongation and stomatal row order, testing whether oblong-cell tissues show stronger row alignment than polygonal-cell tissues and whether minimal partitions mediate the relation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Open images are not evenly sampled across monocots and dicots.

Venation and developmental patterning can independently impose rows.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Row versus scattered arrangement against cell shape is a clear spatial test, and one half of it, scattered stomata on a polygonal epidermis, can be measured from a deposited coordinate table. The oblong-cell, rowed half is widely illustrated and not similarly compiled. Phylogenetic confounding between grasses and files keeps even a future two-sided test from being automatic.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure epidermal cell aspect ratio and the spatial arrangement of stomata on the same leaves. Stomata in rows where cells are oblong, and irregularly placed where cells are polygonal, including within lineages that break the monocot-dicot pairing, would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Monocots tend to have both oblong cells and stomatal files, so phylogeny and cell shape have to be separated.

The open coordinate table is Arabidopsis, a polygonal case, and does not include the oblong-celled monocot leaves that should show rows.
